detailed_rationale:
MSTC Ltd is a Mini Ratna Category-I PSU (under the Ministry of Steel, established 1964) that runs e-auction, e-procurement and trading-facilitation services -- principally metal-scrap trading, coal/mineral-block auctions, and a digital marketplace -- on a largely commission-based model rather than taking principal inventory positions, which explains its structurally high asset turnover and margins.

The trailing growth figures need real care here. Annual revenue collapsed from ~Rs.721cr (Mar 2023) to ~Rs.316cr (Mar 2024) -- a 56% contraction -- before partially recovering to ~Rs.370cr (Mar 2026), which is exactly what shows up in the quant data as a negative 3-year revenue CAGR (~-19.9%) alongside a positive 1-year growth figure (~18.6%) and a growth_divergence_flag. On top of that base-effect distortion, we found a large, genuine one-off: Q4 FY25 carried an exceptional ~Rs.291cr 'other income' figure -- several times larger than the company's typical quarterly operating revenue (~Rs.80-120cr) -- which will have flattered that year's reported profit and ROE substantially; Q4 FY26 carried a smaller but still notable ~Rs.32cr other-income item. This is a textbook case of the skill's earnings-quality one-off hunt: trailing profit/ROE metrics for this name are meaningfully influenced by irregular, large other-income events (plausibly PSU-related items such as arbitration awards, claim recoveries, or investment-income timing) rather than purely core trading-commission economics. On the positive side, debt has fallen sharply (from ~Rs.615cr near the post-IPO peak to ~Rs.145cr now), reducing balance-sheet risk.
recommendation_rationale: Quant recommendation is Hold, and we agree, but with real caution flagged in the qualitative writeup: this is a volatile, government-auction-cadence-dependent commission business whose recent 'growth' partly reflects recovery off a disrupted, unusually low FY24 base plus large, irregular other-income items rather than a clean underlying trend. That volatility argues against treating the trailing growth or ROE figures at face value, but it is a known characteristic of this specific PSU trading-facilitator model rather than a broader methodology gap, so we do not escalate.
summary: MSTC is a government-owned e-auction and trading-facilitation company (metal scrap, coal-block auctions, e-procurement) whose revenue and profit have been quite volatile, including a sharp prior-year revenue collapse and at least one unusually large one-off 'other income' item that inflated a past year's reported profit. Debt has come down significantly, which is a genuine positive. We rate it a Hold: there is a real structural opportunity in India's scrap-recycling and e-auction push, but the earnings history is too lumpy and one-off-influenced to treat the recent growth numbers at face value.
positive_para: MSTC sits at the center of two genuine structural themes -- India's National Steel Scrap Recycling Policy (driving more organized metal-scrap trading through platforms like MSTC) and the continued cadence of government coal/mineral-block e-auctions -- while running an asset-light, commission-based model that requires little capital. Debt has fallen sharply from its post-IPO peak, and the company has clearly reduced balance-sheet risk even as trading volumes have partially recovered.
negative_para: The reported growth and profitability trend is genuinely hard to read cleanly: revenue fell over 50% from FY23 to FY24 before partially recovering, and at least one recent year's profit was materially boosted by an outsized, non-recurring 'other income' item (roughly Rs.291cr in a single quarter versus a typical quarterly revenue base of Rs.80-120cr). A commission-based business this dependent on government auction cadence and periodic one-off items is inherently difficult to underwrite as a steady compounder, and the historical ROE figure should be read with the one-off income contribution discounted.
reverse_dcf_judgment: Given the earnings history includes at least one large, clearly identifiable one-off other-income event, the trailing PE and ROE are not reliable anchors for a reverse-DCF; on a normalized, core-commission-income basis the business is probably worth closer to a modest, single-digit-to-low-teens grower valuation, and we would not treat the current multiple as either clearly cheap or clearly rich without a cleaner multi-year, one-off-adjusted earnings series.
